title: Abraham Buys a Grave for Sarah
overview: When Sarah dies, Abraham, still a foreigner in Canaan, buys a field with a cave to bury her, and it becomes the first piece of the promised land he legally owns.

parts.label: Sarah dies (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Sarah dies at Hebron after more than sixty years of living in Canaan as an outsider. The two words for Abraham's grief likely point to both the customary mourning rites, such as sitting on the ground, and his own real tears.

parts.label: A foreigner asks for a grave (vv. 3-6)
parts.note: Abraham has moved around Canaan for decades but owns no land, so he must ask the local people, called Hittites, for a place to bury his wife. They honor him and offer their best tombs, but a borrowed tomb would not make any ground his own.

parts.label: Bargaining at the city gate (vv. 7-15)
parts.note: The city gate was where public business was done, with the townsmen acting as witnesses. Ephron's offer to give the land is most likely polite bargaining language common in that world, and his casual mention of four hundred shekels quietly names his price, though some readers take his kindness at face value.

parts.label: The deal is sealed (vv. 16-18)
parts.note: There were no coins yet, so Abraham weighs out the silver by the standard merchants used, and many scholars think the price was high. The careful list of field, cave and trees reads like a legal deed, so no one could later dispute that the land was his.

parts.label: Sarah is buried (vv. 19-20)
parts.note: This cave at Machpelah is the only land Abraham ever owns in the country he had been promised. Later in Genesis, Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah and Jacob are buried there too, and the traditional site in Hebron is still honored today.

think: What makes a place truly feel like yours: owning it, living there a long time, or having people you love buried there?
